newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian titanium maker eyes parts for Boeing.
newsitem.headline: Russian titanium maker eyes parts for Boeing.

text.p: Russian titanium producer Verkhne-Saldinsky metallurgical combine on Thursday said U.S. aircraft maker Boeing Co had approved factory stamped titanium output quality and could soon make orders for parts.

Anatoli Tozhkov, a director for quality control, told Reuters that the plant, which has supplied Boeing with primary titanium since 1993, hoped to get new orders for value-added, finished aircraft components soon.

"This August Boeing put our company in its list of official stamped titanium suppliers for their aircraft," Tozhkov said by telephone from a Verkhnya Salda, a small town in the western Asian Ural region of Russia.
The factory plans to make finished parts for Boeing aircraft instead of sending primary metal for stamping or forging into parts in the United States.

"Stamped titanium exports are more profitable and we are trying to get approval certificates for more parts from Boeing," Tozhkov added. He did not say for which components the factory had received approval from Boeing.
He declined to give figures for factory titanium output but said Verkhne-Saldinsky shipped about 60 percent of its exports to Boeing and 40 percent to Airbus Industrie.

Boeing Commercial Airplane Group vice-president Robert Spitzer told Reuters in a recent interview that Russian titanium, used for pilots cabin and engines frames, made up about 15 percent of the titanium used on new Boeing 777s.
Spitzer said Boeing titanium purchases from Russian suppliers were in the millions of dollars annually, and said Verkhne-Saldinsky was a world-leader in titanium production.
Boeing's Commercial Airplane Group worked with 14 Russian aircraft organisations and firms, he said.
Verkhne-Saldinsky used to supply titanium to Russian plane makers, but orders have fallen 15-20 times compared to Soviet-era volumes, Tozhkov said.
